title: Climate Change: Science and the Greenhouse Effect

cards.b:
Climate change links to agriculture, water, energy, security and diplomacy. UPSC asks the science in Prelims and the policy in Mains. A sound base here makes the next eight lessons easy.

Always use the latest numbers and date them.

The topic also connects with geography, such as the monsoon and glaciers, and with economy through energy and agriculture. UPSC asks the basic science, such as the gases, global warming potential and feedbacks, in Prelims. Mains asks for India's position, adaptation and finance. Use IPCC reports as the standard source for evidence, and give the year.

Sunlight warms Earth. Earth sends heat back as long-wave radiation. Greenhouse gases absorb some of it and re-emit it, keeping the planet about 33 °C warmer than it would be. This is natural and needed for life.

The problem is the enhanced greenhouse effect: humans have added gases since the industrial era.

Greenhouse gases are transparent to incoming short-wave sunlight but absorb outgoing long-wave infrared. Without them the average surface temperature would be about minus 18 °C instead of about 15 °C. Water vapour is the strongest natural greenhouse gas, but its amount responds to temperature, so it acts as a feedback rather than a driver. Venus shows a runaway case of the effect.

The six Kyoto gases are CO2, methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), HFCs, PFCs and SF6. Global warming potential (GWP) compares them with CO2 (GWP 1). Methane is about 28 times over 100 years but lasts only about a decade. N2O is about 270 times. SF6 is over 23,000 times.

Water vapour is the biggest natural greenhouse gas but responds to temperature rather than driving it. Black carbon is a short-lived warming agent, not a gas.

The IPCC (set up in 1988 by WMO and UNEP) reported in its Sixth Assessment (2021–23) that human activity has warmed the planet by about 1.1 °C above 1850–1900 levels. CO2 now stands above 420 ppm versus about 280 before industry (as of 2025).

The World Meteorological Organization said 2024 was the first calendar year above 1.5 °C. A single year above 1.5 °C is not the same as the Paris long-term target, which is measured over decades. Sea level rose about 20 cm between 1901 and 2018.

Ice-albedo feedback: melting ice exposes dark sea or land, which absorbs more heat. Permafrost thaw releases methane. Warmer oceans hold less CO2. These loops can push the climate past tipping points such as ice-sheet collapse or Amazon dieback.

Ocean acidification is a related effect: dissolved CO2 lowers pH and harms corals and shellfish.

El Niño warms the eastern Pacific and usually weakens the Indian monsoon. La Niña is the cool phase and usually helps it. The Indian Ocean Dipole can offset El Niño when positive. These cycles cause year-to-year swings; climate change is the long-term trend.

India’s monsoon forecasts depend on these links.

China, the US and India are the top three emitters in recent years in absolute terms. India’s per capita emissions are about half the world average, and its cumulative share is small (under 5 percent).

This is the basis of common but differentiated responsibilities (CBDR-RC): historic emitters should lead.

cards.h: Mitigation or adaptation, and who pays
cards.b:
Developed countries stress cutting emissions everywhere. Developing countries stress adaptation, finance and the right to develop. Some scientists urge carbon removal and geoengineering; others warn of moral hazard.

The carbon budget idea gives a fixed amount of CO2 left for a temperature target. Fair shares are the core of the dispute.

India is highly exposed to heat, floods, monsoon swings and sea-level rise. It has set a net-zero target for 2070 and stresses equity and climate justice.

India is not part of the Global Methane Pledge (2021, 30 percent cut by 2030), citing livestock and rice methane tied to livelihoods.

Mains-style: “Explain the greenhouse effect and the evidence for human-induced climate change. Why is India vulnerable?” Structure: mechanism; gases and GWP; IPCC numbers (dated); India’s exposure; two responses.

Prelims tip: Kyoto has six gases. Methane has higher GWP but shorter life than CO2. IPCC founded 1988. El Niño usually weakens the monsoon.
